correctness.rationale: Exact frozen facet table has 72 five-vertex facets with f-vector (12,60,160,180,72), checked independently from literal script data. A nonzero integral 2-cycle needs >=4 distinct vertices; on four vertices it must be an integer multiple of oriented tetrahedron boundary. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all C(12,4)=495 supports found exactly 60 with all 4 triangular faces present but no tetrahedron. Independently reconstructed both 20-term integral cochains and checked δc=0 on all 180 tetrahedra; all 60 boundary evaluations are ±(1,0) or ±(0,1), distribution 15,15,25,5, giving 30/30 up to sign. As published topology H2(K;Z)=Z², the induced evaluation map onto Z² is an isomorphism, so these are primitive nontrivial H2 classes. Independently closed the two literal generators to group order 240; every group element permutes all 72 facets and one missing-tetrahedron orbit has all 60 elements. Thus shortest support=4, two primitive directions, single symmetry orbit. Exact finite enumeration is exhaustive for this exact finite K, not a claim of all 12-vertex triangulations.

value.rationale: For a canonical highly symmetric triangulation of S2xS2, smallest vertex carriers of integral middle homology form a natural simplicial systolic invariant. The exact 60 minimizers occupy only two primitive directions, all in one 240-element automorphism orbit; this compares geometric support with integral homology and symmetry. The finite complete classification is meaningful as a reusable structural benchmark; it need not generalize to every triangulation.
residual_risks: Specific single finite triangulation and vertex-count support metric; no new general manifold theorem.
